A3.0 Definitions Chief Academic Officer of the Institute The term Chief Academic Officer refers to the individual responsible for all academic (educational and research) programs.

The specific title of the Chief Academic Officer may change from time to time (Dean of the Faculty and Provost have been the most common in the past), at present the Chief Academic Officer is the Chair of the Deans' Council.

Tenure Track (TT) Faculty The term "tenure track faculty member" refers to a full-time member of the teaching faculty of the School carrying the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, or Professor who is either tenured or in a tenure track position.

A person whose rank or title contains any of the words "Lecturer", "Affiliate", "Adjunct", "Research", "Visiting" or any other modifier of "Instructor" or the three professorial ranks cannot be a tenure track faculty member.
No person enrolled for a degree at Stevens may be a regular (tenure track) faculty member.

A3.1 Tenure Track Faculty Responsibilities A TT faculty member, in accepting an appointment, has a principal obligation to identify his or her professional welfare with the welfare of Stevens and the Howe School.
His or her responsibilities include effective teaching and advising, research, scholarly works, service - professional, service - institute and school, work week, and workloads.
The ordering implies no priority of importance, and all items are not necessarily expected to the same degree from each TT faculty member.

A3.1.1 Effective Teaching and Advising This involves adequate and timely preparation for classes, maintenance of high professional standards of quality, participation in regular course evaluation activities, and active participation in academic program committees, advising students on curricular and professional matters, continuous course/program development and seeking outside support for the development of educational programs.

A3.1.2 Research Conducting basic and/or applied research or improving an art. This includes advising thesis and dissertation students, chairing dissertation committees, seeking financial support from outside sources, and keeping abreast of professional developments.
A3.1.3 Scholarly Works Writing and publishing professional papers, textbooks, or other scholarly works.

A3.1.3.1 Designation as Research Faculty Tenure Track members of the faculty will be classified as research faculty if each year they satisfy one of the first two items under the Publications/Research criteria, and one of the four remaining under the Publications/Research criteria and all of the Other Scholarly Activities criteria.
In addition, research faculty will chair Ph.D. dissertation committees in their fields and graduate at least one Ph.D. student every three years.
In addition, research faculty will be encouraged to actively participate in Technogenesis activities.
In each case the annual figure is calculated as a three-year average.

Publications /Research Publish two refereed journal articles, publish one article in a top-tier scholarly journal with a low acceptance rate (e.g., less than 10 percent) or in a journal recognized as one of the leading journals in the field, obtain external research/consulting grants of at least $25,000 in net contribution to the Howe School, publish a book, serve in an editorial capacity or on the editorial board of a scholarly journal, patents applied for or issued.

Other Scholarly Activities Present two refereed conference papers, submit at least one proposal for external support that would provide at least $25,000 net contribution to the Howe School, publish two Stevens working papers on different topics or two book chapters.

A3.1.3.2 Research Faculty Support The Dean may support Research Faculty by providing them summer support (one or two months), a research assistant (RA) and travel expenses to conferences where the faculty member actively participates (e.g., presenting papers, chairing sessions, or serving as an officer).

While the objective of research funding should be to acquire external funds that provide summer support and research assistants, there may be instances where the Dean may invest to obtain future external funding or to accomplish other School goals.

In the case of new faculty on the tenure track, the Dean will normally provide one or two summer months support, a full-time RA and a travel and equipment budget for the initial term of the appointment.

This investment is made with the anticipation that the faculty member will secure external research/consulting funding after the initial term of the appointment to support these expenditures on a continuing basis.

A3.1.4 Service - Professional Participating in outside professional activities appropriate to the above responsibilities at other academic institutions, professional societies, and/or business, charitable and government agencies.

A3.1.5 Service - Institute and School Active participation and leadership on Academic Program, School and Institute committees and in regular scheduled Academic Program, School and Institute functions such as faculty meetings, convocation, and commencement.
A3.1.6 Work Week TT faculty will devote at least five days per week during the semester when they are teaching to discharge the above listed responsibilities.
At least four days per week shall be on campus unless absence is required to fulfill Stevens related responsibilities, in which case the Dean's approval will be obtained.

A3.1.7 Workloads In addition to teaching, research and/or the development and implementation of special educational programs, the workload includes the participation in Academic Program, School or institutional committees and other professional activities as cited in Section 3.1.
Each individual's workload for the year shall be assigned by his or her Program Director as applicable and reviewed by the Office of the Dean.
This workload shall be documented in a plan and submitted to the Office of the Dean by August 1 of each year.
Teaching in executive education is not part of a faculty member's baseline teaching load.
A baseline teaching load shall be twenty-four credits for the year.
TT faculty members performing research and/or other appropriate scholarly activities would not be assigned the baseline teaching load.

The baseline teaching load will be assigned only in those cases where there is no evidence of research activities such as submission of proposals, publication of research papers in refereed journals, publication of textbooks, and presentation of research papers at professional society meetings or other scholarly activities based on the prior year's activities.
A reduced individual teaching load for research, scholarly activities or specific activities directly supporting school growth or other initiatives is granted by the Dean of the School.
The extent of reductions will be commensurate with the individual's level of research, scholarly activities or new initiatives.
Such requests shall be submitted to the Dean for approval.

In addition, a faculty member who is not designated as research faculty and who chairs Ph.D. dissertation committees will receive one course relief each year for every three Ph.D. students for a maximum of two years per student.
In view of their expected research activities, untenured TT faculty are expected to carry a teaching load of 12 credits for the year.
Teaching extra sections for extra compensation by this faculty will be limited to a maximum of two additional course sections per year, unless the Dean grants a waiver.
This extra teaching will be a voluntary choice of the faculty member.
Program directors will not schedule untenured TT faculty to teach additional course sections above the four-course load without concurrence of the faculty member and the Dean's Office.
Tenured faculty who satisfy the criteria of a research faculty member as set forth in section A3.1.3.1 will normally carry a teaching load of twelve credits for the year.

Tenured faculty who meet at least two of the criteria listed under Publications/Research and at least one criterion listed under Other Scholarly Activities will normally carry a teaching load of a total of eighteen credits for the year.

A3.2 Non-Tenure Track Faculty Responsibilities In order to maintain the quality, flexibility, and continuity of the academic activities of the Howe School, the work of the TT faculty may be complemented by the services of other qualified persons engaged in educational activities in positions that confer faculty status.

These non-tenure track faculty positions are full-time members of the School's teaching and research faculty carrying academic ranks of Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, and Executive-in-Residence or professorial ranks with any modifiers (other than Institute or named chairs), including "Research", "Exemplary Service", "Visiting", and "Distinguished Service".
These positions confer faculty status but are not subject to the promotion and tenure policies of the Institute as defined for tenure track faculty.
The various designations identified as non-TT faculty may not be used for any other positions in the Howe School.
These appointments are appropriate only for the performance of educational responsibilities and other responsibilities that are to be certified by a decision of the TT faculty of the School.

These non-tenure track responsibilities are so specifically focused as to be inappropriate for tenure track status; they require the employment of persons of sufficiently high caliber and specific talent as to justify the conferring of faculty status in order to attract and retain them, without requiring of them all of the duties normally expected of TT faculty.

Since the primary duties of most non-TT faculty concern teaching, the main criterion for appointment and promotion is excellence in teaching and other activities directly related to teaching (e.g., course and curriculum development, educational research and executive education).
Faculty members should not be considered for appointment as non-TT faculty merely because attainment of tenure is unlikely.

In some cases, the primary responsibility of non-TT faculty will be participation in the research activities of the School; such faculty members would carry the rank of Research Associate, Visiting Assistant Professor, Visiting Associate Professor, Visiting Professor, or Research Assistant Professor, Research Associate Professor, or Research Professor.
A3.2.1 Teaching/Research A non-TT faculty member, in accepting an appointment, has a principal obligation to identify his or her professional welfare with the welfare of Stevens and the Howe School.

Excellence in teaching is the primary responsibility of the faculty member, including adequate and timely preparation for classes, maintenance of high professional standards of quality, active participation in regular course evaluation activities, participation in course and curriculum development activities, active participation in Academic program committees, and, when appropriate, advising students on curriculum and professional matters.
Non-TT faculty may be asked to assume key roles in school growth or other activities.
Teaching in Executive Education is not part of a faculty member's baseline teaching load.

Research non-TT faculty will be responsible for active participation in the research activities of the School, including publication of scholarly journal articles, books, and working papers; presentations of research to professional societies; the generation of external research funding; and other research initiatives, such as Technogenesis.
A non-TT faculty member will serve on all Academic Program and Howe School committees to which he or she is elected or appointed.
The faculty member is expected to participate in all official functions of his or her Academic Program and Howe School, including faculty meetings.

In addition, when appropriate, the Dean may appoint the faculty member to administrative duties directly related to the School's educational activities, including Course Coordinator, Program Director, or school initiatives such as growth.
Non-TT faculty will devote at least five days per week during the semesters when they teach to discharge the above-listed responsibilities.
At least four days per week shall be on campus unless absence is required to fulfill Stevens-related responsibilities, in which case the Dean's approval will be obtained.
The baseline teaching load shall be twenty-four credits for the year.
It is expected that non-TT faculty members performing substantial administrative activities, such as Program Director, will not be assigned the baseline teaching load.
The baseline teaching load would be assigned only in those cases where the faculty member's activities consist solely of teaching and teaching-related activities.

The Dean of the School will grant a reduced individual teaching load for a non-TT faculty member who is performing substantial administrative activities or activities directly related to new school initiatives.
The extent of reductions will be commensurate with the individual's activities.
Executive education activities should not be considered as fulfilling a faculty member's baseline teaching responsibilities.
Non-TT faculty who meet the criteria for research faculty, as set forth in section A3.1.3.1, will normally carry a teaching load of at most twelve credits for the academic year.

All appointments and reappointments to non-TT faculty positions, and the specification of their term of employment and compensation arrangement, are made by the Office of the Dean in consultation with individual Program Directors.
The initial appointment for Lecturers will be for one year.
For Senior Lecturers, Executives-in-Residence, and professorial ranks, the initial appointment can be for one to two years.

Candidates for non-TT faculty positions should ideally possess a doctoral degree in their field, such as a PhD or J.D.

Quality Assurance for the Howe School Educational Programs Introduction: The purpose of this policy is to outline the process required to ensure the quality of the educational programs in the Howe School.
Most of the actions suggested are practiced by some schools some of the time.
All the actions suggested were practiced by Stevens at one time or another.
However, because of our growth, fewer and fewer of these practices are being employed.
The result has impacted the quality of the programs and benefits to the students and companies.
Another problem in academe is that the customer/supplier model does not work well, which thwarts continuous process improvement.
For example, most individual students or their companies do not see course/teacher evaluations (except in some off-campus programs) and rarely provide suggestions for continuous improvement.
We do not survey companies, faculty, or alumni on a regular basis.

Quality of Graduate Programs: To ensure that the undergraduate and graduate programs are of superior quality and in the top 5% of programs in the US, all the actions suggested should be practiced all of the time.
This requires a continual commitment of people and financial resources.
The approach described below recognizes the customer/supplier relationship and provides a number of opportunities for it to work.
Advisory Committees: Accreditation guidelines recommend that all major educational programs and/or disciplines have advisory/steering committees.
The purpose of the Advisory Committee is to help establish the vision, mission, and strategic objectives; oversee the program and support suggestions for improvements.
These committees usually consist of the program's customers.
In some cases, it would be the Stevens Alliance for Technology Management (SATM).
In other cases, these would be interested professional groups and/or distinguished alumni.
In addition, some members could be experts in the field or related fields that could provide insight into academic theory and practice.
Typically, Advisory Committees consist of five to nine members and meet once or twice a year.

Meetings usually consist of listening to presentations on curriculum, course development, feedback from students/faculty, faculty development, student recruitment, etc., summaries of all the major topics associated with establishing and running an educational program.
The Advisory Committees are expected to evaluate and comment on the items presented.
Some Advisory Committees are more proactive and help formulate programs, recruit faculty and students, and even raise money.
Overall, the Advisory Committee is concerned with policy and to see that the program is well run.

From a quality perspective, the Advisory Committee can serve as the ultimate customer (companies) and provide feedback and suggestions for improvement based on the information received from the Program Director/Academic Committee.
To make Advisory Committee meetings meaningful, relevant reports and/or recommendations should be sent out before meetings with a detailed agenda.
Advisory Committee meetings should have them for the members to provide feedback on their companies/students' needs.
Proposals should be voted upon to assure participation of the Advisory Committee members.
Academic Committees/Program Directors: Every educational program should have an academic team of experienced and knowledgeable professionals responsible for its development and operation.
ABET (Accrediting Board for Engineering and Technology) and other groups (AACSB, etc.) usually recommend a minimum of three full-time regular (tenure track) faculty.
Whenever possible, the entire regular tenure track faculty should be members of the Academic Committee where they teach courses.
All the course coordinators should also be members.
The Program Director should be a full-time tenure track Professor in the Wesley J.
Howe School of Technology Management when possible.
This team would be responsible for the evaluation, development, and operation of the program.
Key functions would include assessing the student course/teacher evaluations, obtaining company input, assessing course and program development, advising students, and the administrative details.
The Academic Committee should regularly report to the Advisory Committee its findings and suggestions for improvement.
The Stevens faculty members would be responsible to ensure that all actions are consistent with Institute practice.
Course Coordinators: Every course should have a course coordinator.
Course coordinators are responsible for the course outline to ensure that the course is articulated in the curriculum.
Howe School of Technology Management is responsible for establishing a common survey instrument, its implementation, and analysis of results.
The key will be the assessment of the result by the academic committee and their suggestions for improvement.
This will occur at least three times a year after classes end.
Recommendations could include changes in topics, text, and teachers.
Company/Faculty/Alumni Surveys: The academic committee will be responsible for developing the survey instrument, its implementation, and analysis of results.
Other means of obtaining feedback should be encouraged.
Affiliate Buddies: Most graduate programs in management or business use a large number of adjuncts from industry.
Howe School of Technology Management follows this pattern.
In order to ensure that these adjuncts meet all the requirements expected of them, a full Stevens faculty member would be their "buddy."
This will involve sitting in on the adjunct's class, reviewing course outlines, etc. The adjunct buddy is usually the course coordinator.
Course Outlines: For each class, a course outline with appropriate references, projects, grading, etc. will be submitted to the Academic Committees.
The Academic Committees review this outline and provide guidance to the individual teacher.
A summary report and suggestions for improvement will be presented to the Advisory Committee at least once a year.

Course and Program Development via Case Studies, Educational Threads, Software, Library: The Academic Committee needs to periodically review and suggest modifications to existing courses and development of case studies, educational threads, software, library resources, and references used for this program.
A summary report and suggestions for improvement will be presented to the Advisory Committee at least once a year.

Summary: Organization Structure: Advisory Committee: Stevens Alliance for Technology Management (SATM), interested professional organizations, company representatives, and students; Academic Committee: Stevens full-time faculty who teach courses in the program, all course coordinators, regular tenure track; Academic Program Director: Stevens full-time faculty member; Course Coordinators: SIT full-time faculty member, tenure track preferred; Affiliate Buddies: Stevens full-time faculty member, tenure track preferred.

Tools: Analyses: By Whom: Curriculum description critique by faculty, review by AC; Course outlines critique by faculty, review by AC; Course/teacher evaluations suggestions by faculty, review by AC/AdC; Observation of teaching critique by program director; Company/faculty/alumni survey results reviewed by AC and AdC; Course/program development based on surveys, implemented by AC.
Customers: Suppliers: Students, alumni, companies; teachers via course, program.

The major deliverables from the annual review process are a recommendation for salary adjustment for each faculty member, an Annual Review Letter from the dean to each faculty member containing praise and thanks, and/or suggestions for improving performance as appropriate, and salary recommendations and metrics on faculty performance for the President.
The steps are as follows: Step 1 - August 15 The Dean's Office will distribute the Annual Review Report to each Howe School faculty member.
The Annual Review Report consists of a pro-forma Activity Report and Metrics Data Sheet for the last academic year together with a plan for the faculty member's activities in the following year.

Step 2 - before September 15 The Dean's Office collects the Annual Review Reports from each faculty member and distributes copies of the Annual Reviews to each Program Director for their direct reports.
Step 3 - Before September 30 Program Directors use the above material in review sessions with each faculty member in their program.
The purpose of these sessions is to discuss the faculty member's contribution and potential contribution to the Director's Program.
At the end of the meeting, the Director and the faculty member will review the written notes taken during the meeting.

These notes can be very brief but should contain a list of items where the faculty member has done well, a similar list where improvements might be made, and a list of suggestions or concerns of the faculty member regarding his or her involvement in the program.
Step 4 - Before October 15 Program Directors meet individually with the Associate Dean for Research and Academics to review the teaching and service performance of all faculty in their program.

Step 5 - Before November 7 The Associate Dean meets with all tenure track and research-oriented faculty members to review their research output for the year and plans to increase research productivity in the following years.
At the end of the meeting, the Associate Dean and the faculty member should agree on the written notes taken during the meeting.

Step 6 - Before November 14 The Associate Dean meets with each Program Director to review the faculty in each Program Area and to agree on a set of recommendations for each faculty member both with regard to the faculty member's overall performance and specific actions that may need to be taken for improvement of individual faculty members in the following year.

Step 7 - Before November 7 The Dean and Associate Dean meet with all faculty members not directly reporting to any Program Director and go through the same process as the Program Directors with their own faculty.

Step 9 - Before November 21 The Dean meets with each Program Director to discuss plans and provide feedback.
The Associate Dean will be present during the first half of this meeting, which should be devoted to directions for the Director's program and its relationship to the strategic plan.
Step 10 - Before November 21 The Dean goes through a similar process with all his direct reports in the Dean's Office.
Step 11 - Before December 7 The Dean discusses all salary recommendations and faculty metrics with the President.
Step 12 - December 10 The deadline by which the Dean shall have notified Program Directors of his or her decisions.
Step 13 - Before December 15 The annual review letters are sent to individual faculty.

3.23 Ownership and Management of Intellectual Property - Office of Academic Affairs Syracuse University Syracuse University is dedicated to teaching, research, and the dissemination of knowledge.

When these activities have been supported by the University and have resulted in the creation of properties that have economic interest and value, Syracuse University will retain title to, or have a fair and equitable income interest proportional to the Universitys investment in, those properties that will reflect the legitimate interest of University investment as well as the traditions of academic freedom and pursuit.

Members of the University: For the purpose of this policy, members of the University are defined as faculty, staff, students, or any person performing research or engaging in work or study utilizing University resources or facilities, whether or not they are compensated for their services.

Technology: For the purposes of this policy, technology denotes inventions, discoveries, creations, technical innovations, information in various forms, including computer software, and tangible research property created in the course of research.
Tangible research property includes, but is not limited to, notes, sketches, drawings, results of research or experiments, computer code or records, or any embodiment of the technology into any form.
For purposes of this policy, technology does not include any copyright publication.

Title and Interest in Copyright Publications: Title to any copyright publication belongs to the member who has created the copyright publication, except in the case when it has been created under a sponsored program where there are ownership restrictions or in the case the copyright publication was created as part of a members explicit work assignment.
Copyright publication includes, without limitation, written and artistic materials such as articles, books, compilations, and visual and performing art works, whether or not protected by copyright.
Under this policy, copyright publication does not include software.
Generally Available Resources and University Allocated Resources: For the purposes of this policy, generally available resources refer to office space, library, and traditional desktop computers.
In addition, the University will construe salary paid from regularly budgeted department accounts as generally available resources.

In those cases where salary was paid to accomplish or produce certain tasks or materials that were part of the members work assignment with the University or a part of a sponsored program, that salary is considered a University allocated resource.
Other University allocated resources refer to all University resources and facilities that have not been defined as generally available resources.

Technology Resulting from Research Supported with Externally Sponsored or University Allocated Resources: Title to technology resulting from research, work, or study which was supported by externally sponsored or University allocated resources will belong to Syracuse University.

Any revenue received by the University as a result of the license or transfer of such technology will be distributed to those who created the technology in accordance with the paragraph, Distribution of Revenue (below).
The University may transfer its interest in the technology to a member, a members corporation, or an organization with which a member has significant financial ties.
In this situation, a license agreement will be negotiated between that member or organization and the University.

Technology Resulting from Research Supported with Generally Available University Resources: Title to technology except technology identified in the previous paragraph, resulting from research, work, or study solely supported with generally available resources, will belong to the member; and the University will have an equitable interest in the net revenue realized from the income, sale, or transfer of the technology.

When the technology identified under this paragraph is transferred or licensed by a member to a third party or is retained by the member for his or her economic development, a royalty agreement will be negotiated between Syracuse University and the member.
The royalty and license agreement will reflect the Universitys investment in the technology.

Committee on Intellectual Property: The Vice President for Research appoints a Committee on Intellectual Property including faculty from diverse academic units, at least one academic professional staff member, and at least one student.
A normal term for service will be three years with membership renewable for one term.
The Senior Vice President for Business and Finance and the Vice President for Research will serve on the committee as ex officio members.
A senior member of the faculty serves as chair of the committee.
The committee advises the Vice President for Research on the interpretation, administration, and implementation of this policy.
Any appeals of the decisions of the Vice President for Research are directed to the Chancellor.

Distribution of Revenue from Technology: Net revenue defined as gross revenues less the costs and expenses incurred and related to the securing of legal protection, marketing, licensing, and other expenses associated with the technology received by the University from the transfer, sale, or licensing of technology is distributed as follows: Fifteen percent of net revenues will be retained by the University in support of its costs in managing its intellectual property program.

The remaining net revenues will be distributed 50 percent to the inventor or creator and 50 percent to the University in accordance with the Universitys schedule for calculating and dispersing distributable net revenues.

The Universitys share of distributable net revenues will be used for the support of the department or unit of the inventor or creator, development of new intellectual property, or to support the general research and scholarly goals of the University.

Modification of the standard distribution of distributable net revenue may be made in consideration of extenuating circumstances, including but not limited to proportion of royalties retained personally by inventor or creator, extent of investment by all parties, and the additional support needed for further development of the technology.
Any modification of the standard distribution of royalties will be made by the Vice President for Research in consultation with the Committee on Intellectual Property.

Management of University Technology: The Office of Sponsored Programs has the primary responsibility within Syracuse University for managing and administering matters involving technology developed at Syracuse.
The Office of Sponsored Programs will consult with members regarding the best means for development and transfer of the technology created by members.

It may be necessary, in accordance with the terms of this policy, that any assignments, licenses, transfers, applications, registrations, or any other documents that are necessary to evidence the Universitys ownership in technology be executed by members.

Disclosure: Under some United States and foreign laws, public disclosure, use, or sale of technology prior to obtaining statutory protection may prejudice, or destroy, the availability of obtaining certain legal protection.

In order to protect the Universitys, members, or any licensees rights in technology, no contractual or other legally enforceable agreement for the sale, transfer, or use of University-owned technology may be made except by the University in accordance with this policy.
It is also essential to consult with OSP prior to making any technology publicly known or available.

Limited License in All Technology Created by Members: Notwithstanding any other provision of this policy, Syracuse University maintains a royalty-free, nonexclusive, and nontransferable license to use for noncommercial purposes for teaching, training, and research with the University, all technology created by its members.
Good Faith: The fair and effective implementation of this policy requires good faith cooperation, collegiality, and candor on behalf of Syracuse University and all of its members.
For its part, the University will seek to advise affected members promptly and fully on all matters regarding technology.
Members, in turn, will communicate promptly and fully with OSP whenever their research involves technology covered by the policy.
Amendment: This policy may be amended from time to time pursuant to the Universitys policies and procedures in effect for amending documents setting forth University policy.
Drafted by the Senate Research Committee and approved by the Chancellor as interim policy July 13, 1992.

POLICIES AND PROCEDURES MANUAL Title: Invention and Patent Policy Policy Number: 02.53.01 Effective Date: March 12, 1985 Issuing Authority: Board of Trustees Policy The following policy was adopted by the Board of Trustees on March 12, 1985, and supersedes all previous issuances.

PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES As a part of its mission as a comprehensive educational research institution, Temple University encourages the search for new knowledge, discoveries and inventions which will serve the public good.

In support of this mission, this invention policy sets forth the following objectives: To provide incentive for those engaged in research and the applied arts to commercialize their inventions, to provide a means to commercialize applied technologies, and to define the obligations of all parties involved in the invention process and to safeguard their rights and interests.

OWNERSHIP The University shall be entitled to obtain the entire right, title and interest to any invention (including computer-related software and ancillary materials, but not including pure works of art or musical compositions) which is developed in whole or in part by any University employee, including, without limitation, faculty, staff member, fellow, resident, graduate student or assistant (whether paid or unpaid), which emerges from any University research or development activity, or from use of any University facilities or equipment.
Where such title is held, the University shall assume all control and responsibility for costs and liability of patent prosecution, maintenance and enforcement, if any, and licensing.

Where ownership questions arise due to multi-institutional employment by a person covered by this policy, such question shall be referred to the President or person designated by the President for resolution.

Ownership rights to inventions emerging from activity pursuant to an agreement with an outside sponsor shall be determined in accordance with that agreement, or, in the absence of a controlling agreement, with rules and regulations, if any, governing that sponsorship.

In particular, the University shall be governed by Public Law 96-517, Government Patent Policy Act of 1980 (and any successor thereto or similar laws) and its attendant regulations and amendments regarding federal research agreements.
In all cases, where feasible, the University shall seek to negotiate agreements which permit the University to retain ownership rights.

An inventor shall be entitled to all right, title and interest to any discovery or invention which is developed wholly on the inventor's own time and with the inventor's own facilities and which does not involve use of any University funds, equipment, facilities or personnel.

Where such right, title and interest are claimed and agreed upon, the University shall not assume any responsibility for costs or liability of patent prosecution, maintenance or enforcement or licensing.
An inventor who is entitled to all ownership rights may petition the University to accept assignment of those rights and the attendant control and responsibilities.
The University is under no obligation to accept such assignment, but shall evaluate and act on the petition in view of the objectives of this policy.
The University may elect to waive its ownership rights and release them to the inventor.
Such a waiver by the University shall occur in writing within two months after written disclosure by the inventor to the University.
Where such a waiver occurs, the University shall incur no further expenses and shall assume no liability related to the invention.

In accordance with long-standing academic tradition, the University shall waive its ownership rights in all cases where the invention or software embodies a textbook, article, thesis or other similar item, the intended purpose of which is to disseminate the results of academic research or scholarly study.

Any faculty or staff member, fellow, resident, student or volunteer at the University is responsible for ensuring that any third-party agreement that he or she enters conforms in all respects with the University Invention and Patent Policy or that such agreement has been approved by the Invention and Patent Committee if it does not conform in all respects with University Invention and Patent Policy.

RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE INVENTOR AND THE UNIVERSITY When an invention has been developed under conditions described above in "Ownership" and is deemed by the inventor worthy of evaluation, the inventor has the following responsibilities: To report such invention promptly to the Associate Provost for Research or other office designated by the President as responsible for inventions, where the inventor intends to publish information or make any other public disclosure related to the invention, to notify the office designated in the previous clause of the intention prior to making such public disclosure; the foregoing clause shall not be construed to infringe on anyone's right to publish, to provide full disclosure in writing of such invention to the Associate Provost for Research or other designated office in the manner prescribed by that office, where University rights exist to the invention, to execute all appropriate assignments to the University and to execute all documents necessary to the prompt prosecution of the patent or to the maintenance and enforcement of the patent, to cooperate with the University or its designees in filing, maintaining and enforcing the patent and in all licensing matters, and to provide other reasonable support to assure that patent, licensing or other rights are adequately protected as required by the University.

Upon notice that an invention has been developed, the University has the following responsibilities: To provide prompt technical and legal guidance in the development of a full disclosure, to determine ownership in accordance with section 2 of this policy, where the University is entitled to ownership rights, to decide expeditiously upon the method for administering the invention which best fulfills the objectives of this policy, including whether the University will apply for a patent itself or use an external patent management organization or individual, or whether it will waive rights to the invention and release them to the inventor, where it is determined that patenting is inappropriate but that a commercial market may exist for an invention to which the University has rights, to assist in seeking licensing or other agreements for the invention, where the University elects to seek a patent, to assume all costs associated with patent prosecution, maintenance and enforcement, and to seek and negotiate licensing or other agreements for inventions to which the University has rights, with consultation with the inventor or a representative, and to assume all costs associated therewith.

INCOME DISTRIBUTION The net income to the University from a royalty agreement or other agreement resulting from an invention shall be distributed as follows: 50% to the Inventor(s) and 50% to the University, provided that the inventor(s)' share shall not fall below five percent of the University's gross receipts.

Net income is defined as gross income minus the patenting, legal and marketing costs incurred by the University related to such invention, including as a cost any income share that may be retained by an outside patent management organization.
A statement of such costs, to the extent available to the University, shall be issued to the inventor(s) yearly.

If more than one inventor has contributed to the invention, those inventors shall be allocated equal amounts of the share to the inventors, unless they otherwise jointly instruct the University in writing.
Where the inventors are unable to agree on the subdivisions of their share, they may request a hearing before the Invention and Patent Committee, whose decision shall be final.
The inventor is entitled to the full share of income even if he or she is no longer affiliated with the University.
If the inventor should die, royalties due shall be paid to his or her estate or designee for the duration of the royalty period.
Income earned by the University shall be used to stimulate research.

The first $500,000 of the University's share of royalties from each invention shall be allocated within the University as follows: thirty-five percent to the Department or research Unit responsible for the invention, fifteen percent to the School or College responsible for the invention, and fifty percent to the University.
The distribution of the funds in the previous clauses shall be used as a research supplement to the respective Units' budgets.

Where there is more than one Department, Research Unit, School or College responsible for the invention, the Invention and Patent Committee shall allocate the Universitys share of royalties according to the relative contributions of the inventors to the invention.
The Invention and Patent Committee's allocation decisions shall be final.

OWNERSHIP All persons subject to this policy hereby assign to the university the entire right, title and interest to any invention (including computer-related software and ancillary materials, but not including pure works of art or musical compositions) which is developed in whole or in part by any university employee, including, without limitation, faculty, staff member, fellow, resident, graduate student or assistant (whether paid or unpaid), which emerges from any university research or development activity, or from use of any university facilities or equipment.

Where ownership questions arise due to multi-institutional employment by a person covered by this policy, such question shall be referred to the president or person designated by the president for resolution.

Ownership rights to inventions emerging from activity pursuant to an agreement with an outside sponsor shall be determined in accordance with that agreement, or, in the absence of a controlling agreement, with rules and regulations, if any, governing that sponsorship.

Such a waiver by the university shall occur in writing within two months after written disclosure by the inventor to the university.
Where such a waiver occurs, the university shall incur no further expenses and shall assume no liability related to the invention.

In accordance with long-standing academic tradition, the university shall waive its ownership rights in all cases where the invention or software embodies a textbook, article, thesis or other similar item, the intended purpose of which is to disseminate the results of academic research or scholarly study.

C.10.3 Inventions and Patents The Texas A&M University System Administrative Policy and Reporting Manual Subject: Inventions and Patents C.10.3 July 2, 1991 Page 1 of 8 Contact for Interpretation: Office of General Counsel 1.
Definitions As used in this policy, the following terms shall have the meanings contained herein.

1.1 Invention: intellectual property of all types (including, but not limited to, any invention, discovery, trade secret, technology, scientific or technological development, or patentable computer software) regardless of whether subject to protection under statutory or common law.
1.2 Inventor: an individual or group of individuals who make, conceive, reduce to practice, author, or otherwise contribute to the creation of an invention.

1.3 Intellectual Property Committee: a standing committee appointed by the Chancellor of The Texas A&M University System (the System) representing various components of the System whose purpose is to provide a forum for discussion of policies and procedures affecting inventions, patents, and other issues affecting intellectual properties and advise the Chancellor and Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) regarding intellectual property matters.

1.4 System Intellectual Property Office: a System Administrative Office under the direction of the Deputy Chancellor for External Affairs and General Counsel whose functions are to assist and advise the System components and the System Intellectual Property Committee, provide technical assistance relating to intellectual property covered by this policy, and administer the System Intellectual Property Program.

Statement of Policy The System has a responsibility for and an interest in the advancement of scientific knowledge and creative work that will enhance its educational mission and benefit the public it serves.

The purpose of this policy is threefold: to encourage the development of inventions for the best interest of the public, the creator, and the research sponsor; to provide timely disclosure and protection of such inventions whether by development, commercialization, or publication, or any combination thereof; and to allow employees of the System maximum scientific and professional freedom with respect to the method of disclosure and publication of their findings, consistent with any contractual obligations of employment.

Applicability 3.1 Personnel This policy is applicable to all persons employed by the component institutions and agencies of the System and persons using the System facilities under the supervision of System personnel.
Inventors shall be permitted maximum freedom with respect to their inventions, consistent with the obligations to the System.

Any person affected by this policy who as a result of his or her activities creates an invention (other than governmental or other sponsored research projects where individual grant agreements provide otherwise) will consult with the System in determining how it is to be disclosed to the public.
Present and prospective employees of the System shall, upon request, execute an invention agreement in a form similar to Attachment B to this policy.
Executed invention agreements shall be maintained by the Personnel Offices of the respective System components.
All System employees are required to abide by their obligations and those of the System under research agreements with sponsors.

3.2 Property This policy shall apply to all inventions created under the following conditions: an invention resulting from activities related to an individual's employment responsibilities and/or with support from System administered funds, facilities, or personnel.
An invention unrelated to an individual's employment responsibilities that is developed on his or her own time and without System support or use of System facilities.
Inventions such as this are not owned by the System.

Offers of Inventions: If an individual chooses to offer to the System an invention to which the System has no claim, the System may accept ownership of the invention provided that the individual makes the offer through one of the System components as if the invention had been created within the System, and the individual agrees to all provisions (including royalty provisions) of this policy.

The CEOs of the System components shall advise the Deputy Chancellor for External Affairs and General Counsel of all such offers and will inform the System concerning acceptance or rejection of the offers and intentions for patenting and commercialization.

In cases in which the individual has already expended funds toward obtaining patent or other legal protection for the invention, the individual and the System, or the System component, may negotiate and enter into an agreement allowing recovery of legal and/or patent expenses from license fees and/or royalty income.
Such an agreement would modify normal royalty sharing provisions until such expenses are recovered by the party entitled to recovery of the expenses.

If an inventor offers his or her invention to the System as described in 3.2.3, after obtaining patent or other protection, similar procedures will be followed in deciding whether or not to reimburse the inventor for expenses in obtaining such protection.

3.3 Sponsored Research An invention resulting from research supported by a grant or contract with the Federal Government (or an agency thereof), a nonprofit or for-profit nongovernmental entity, or by a private gift or grant to the System, shall be subject to ownership by the System.
The requirement of System ownership may be amended or varied by written approval of the CEOs, or their designees, when the value received justifies such variance.

In the event of conflict, the intellectual property policies of the System are subject to, and thus amended and superseded by, the specific terms pertaining to invention rights included in such grants or contracts.

Disclosure, Assignment, and Protection All persons subject to this policy shall promptly disclose to their CEO, by use of an invention disclosure form (Attachment A), any invention covered by this policy (including those made under cooperative arrangements).
Such persons shall cooperate in protecting intellectual property rights.
A copy of the disclosure shall be provided to the System Intellectual Property Office.

If the System component or the System decides to patent or seek other available protection for intellectual property, it shall proceed either through its own efforts or those of an appropriate private firm or attorney to obtain protection and/or manage the intellectual property.
4.1 Assignment Documentation All inventors shall execute appropriate assignment and/or other documents required to set forth effectively the ownership and rights to inventions.
4.2 Review of Disclosure All disclosures shall be submitted to the CEO of the System component administering the research or other work from which the invention developed.
The CEO may request a recommendation from the Intellectual Property Committee regarding the disposition of the invention.
The CEO will determine whether the System component desires to commit funding to obtain protection for the intellectual property, or otherwise make use of the invention.

In those instances where delay would jeopardize obtaining the appropriate protection for the invention, the inventor may make a request that the System component expedite its decision as to whether or not it shall proceed to file a patent application or take other steps to obtain available protection.

4.3 Obtaining Protection If, in the judgment of the CEO, it is in the best interest of the System component to obtain and maintain protection for a disclosed invention, he or she shall notify the inventor and the System Intellectual Property Office of such fact.
If the CEO decides that it is not in the best interest of the System component to obtain protection, he or she shall inform the Chancellor or his/her designee of such decision.

If, in the opinion of the Chancellor or his/her designee, it is in the best interest of the System to obtain protection for an invention, he or she may designate a source of funds other than those under the control of the CEO to be used to pay the expenses of obtaining protection.
The Chancellor and the CEO may agree to jointly provide funding to obtain protection for inventions.
Agreements relating to the development and/or commercialization of inventions may provide that the contracting entity bear the costs of obtaining protection for inventions.

Agreements to Develop and/or Commercialize Inventions 5.1 Negotiation of Agreements C.10.3 Inventions and Patents Agreements permitting a party to use, develop, or otherwise commercialize System-owned intellectual property are generally encouraged.
The CEOs of the System components, or their designees, and the System Intellectual Property Office may negotiate with parties having an interest in such activities.

Execution of Agreements Any agreement to license or transfer ownership of System-owned intellectual property by means of a sale, assignment, or exchange shall be submitted to the Board of Regents for approval.
The Chancellor may execute assignments and other instruments required to obtain patent protection in foreign countries.

DISTRIBUTION OF INCOME FROM COMMERCIALIZATION AND LICENSING All monetary proceeds from commercialization of System-owned inventions, including royalties, equity interests, and dividends are the property of the System.

Income received by the System from commercialization of an invention will be distributed as follows: Deduct the costs of obtaining legal protection for the invention to arrive at "adjusted income" (when such costs are not provided from other sources).
When there is no adjusted income after deduction of costs, see Guaranteed Minimum to Inventor(s) below.
Deduct fifteen percent (15%) from adjusted income.
This deduction is directed toward covering the expenses (excluding patent expenses) for administering the System Intellectual Property Office.
Distribute the remaining adjusted income as follows: Fifty percent (50%) to the inventor.
In case of multiple inventorship, the inventors will mutually agree among themselves on the distribution of this portion of the income.
NOTE: For purposes of this policy, "costs" shall mean documented expenses related to patenting the invention and/or documented expenses related to enforcing patent rights against infringement.
Also, when patent law requires the deposit of cultures or organisms with an approved depository, fees charged by the depository shall be deducted as patent expenses.
Faculty members should keep in mind that patent attorneys normally bill by the hour and in as little as 1/10 hour increments.
Contacts with patent attorneys should be made only when necessary so as to keep patenting costs to a minimum.

Guaranteed Minimum to Inventor(s) When there is no adjusted income after deduction of costs in Step 1 or when the inventor's (inventors') portion of the adjusted income is less than 20% of the gross income, the inventor(s) will receive an amount equal to 20% of the gross.

Under these circumstances, the inventor's (inventors') share will be subtracted from gross income and any adjusted income will be distributed fifteen percent (15%) to the System Intellectual Property Office and the remainder to the System component from which the discovery or invention originated.
When the inventor's (inventors') portion of adjusted income is equal to or greater than 20% of gross income, the distribution will be as described in steps 2 and 3 of 6.1.

EQUITY AND OTHER NON-MONETARY RETURNS The System or System component may negotiate, but shall not be obligated to negotiate, for equity interests in lieu of or in addition to royalty and/or monetary consideration as a part of an agreement between the System or System component and a business entity relating to System-owned inventions.
Equity for Inventors Inventors may receive up to fifty percent (50%) of any equity or other non-monetary consideration received by the System under this section.
However, the System may choose to receive the consideration under terms that restrict its ability to sell, distribute, or otherwise deal with the equity interests.
In such cases, any restrictions on the System's interest shall be equally applicable to the interest of the inventor, unless waived or varied in writing and signed by the CEO and the inventor.
No Fiduciary Status The System does not act as a fiduciary for any person concerning equity or other consideration received under the terms of this policy.

Equity Ownership by Inventors Inventors should consult APRM Section B.4.12, FACULTY CONSULTING, OUTSIDE PROFESSIONAL EMPLOYMENT, AND CONFLICTS OF INTEREST, regarding the System policy and State law in the area of equity ownership.
PROVISIONS FOR RELEASE OF RIGHTS TO AN INVENTION The System may release to the inventor(s) its rights to an invention, with the following provisions.
The System shall retain for itself and its components, a perpetual royalty-free license to use the invention and any corresponding patents for research, education, and service purposes.

The System shall receive a share of all proceeds generated from commercialization of the invention after the inventor has recovered documented out-of-pocket costs for obtaining legal protection for the invention.
The System's share shall be negotiated on a case-by-case basis.
Inventor shall not be entitled to a share of proceeds received by the System.
